description: Waits up to 15 seconds for an aicut generation to reach a terminal state, WITHOUT opening a card, and returns the compact status. SEVERAL ITEMS: quote each, ask once with the total, start them all (images with `wait: false`, distinct `idempotency_key`s or none), then make ONE call with `ids` (1 to 6 of `{id, media}`) instead of `id` and `media`. `terminal` is always present: `true` means nothing further arrives on its own (the job is `succeeded` or `failed`, or `awaiting_user` is set); `false` means it is still `queued` or `processing`. WHEN: right after `generate_video`, `generate_image`, `generate_audio` or a transform, and again AT ONCE every time it answers `terminal: false` (same `id` and `media`): it blocks up to 15 seconds itself, so you never sleep or set a timer. Do NOT call it after `generate_story_video` or `fire_story_video` (the card follows those); wait only after `render_story_video`. Do not switch to `get_*` or narrate each attempt: several calls in a row is the expected shape. STALL: no `terminal: true` after about 10 minutes, tell the user so and make ONE `get_*` read of that job. On `terminal: true` say ONE short line about what came out and stop (the card is up: do NOT call `show_generation`); on `failed`, tell the user what went wrong (`error.message`). No card on your client (a terminal)? Give the user the `url`. WITH `ids` it returns when ALL are terminal or the 15 seconds end: `results` (each job in order, with its own `terminal`, `awaiting_user` and `next_step`; an id not on this account gets its own `error` and never fails the rest), `all_terminal` (your loop condition) and, while false, `poll_after_seconds`. Next call: only the jobs still `terminal: false`. A STORY EPISODE PARKED FOR THE USER (`story.stage` `frames_review` or `ready_to_render`) answers `terminal: true` with `awaiting_user: true`: stop waiting, say what is ready and let them decide (a redraw, a fire and a render each need their own priced go). THE ONE EXCEPTION: `ready_to_render` with `story.auto_render: true` is NOT a decision (the fire armed the render, which starts by itself): it answers `terminal: false`, so keep waiting on that render, and if it has not started after a few minutes tell the user and offer `render_story_video`. A render ends at `story.stage: "rendered"` (`story.render.url` is the final file) or, if it failed and was refunded, `awaiting_user: true`. At `ready_to_render` the `url` is only the raw scene preview. Spends no tokens and creates nothing. It returns JSON for you to read: say nothing to the user between waits and never paste it.

id.description: A job id from a `generate_*` tool or transform, or an episode id from `generate_story_video` (media `video`).

ids.description: Several jobs at once (see SEVERAL ITEMS), instead of `id` and `media`.

media.description: Which kind of generation the id belongs to: `video` (a `generate_video` job, any video transform: `upscale_video`, `extend_video`, `edit_video`, `motion_control`, `generate_lipsync`, and a story render; an AI Video Story episode is a `video`), `image` (including `upscale_image`) or `audio`.

name: wait_for_generation
title: Wait for a generation to finish
